question: Can the audited parameterized inherited carrier (distill_parameterized -> resolve -> execute with known-negative refusal) be landed into the shipped kernel (src/spider/kernel.py) through the sanctioned promotion path, such that after promotion the shipped execution path contains a concrete parameterized mechanism that an inherited procedure visibly instantiates and executes on held-out identifiers, together with a companion known-negative refusal certificate?
hypothesis: The audited kernel implementation from EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064/EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 (git blob b15ed848, sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72), when promoted into src/spider/kernel.py via the sanctioned promotion workflow, will enable the shipped kernel to: (1) induce parameterized mechanisms via distill_parameterized from training observations on resource-A identifiers; (2) resolve and execute those mechanisms on never-observed resource-B identifiers with success_rate >= 0.80; (3) correctly refuse known-negative cases (out-of-support identifiers, wrong intent, missing required parameters) with bound_action=null and correctly categorized refusal reasons; while the literal distill() baseline (confidence 0.5 < min_confidence 0.8) continues to be refused on all parameterized tasks.
falsifier: Any of: (1) The sanctioned promotion path cannot be completed (code does not land in src/spider/kernel.py, or promotion validation fails); (2) After promotion, the shipped kernel's distill_parameterized fails to induce a mechanism from >=2 consistent training observations; (3) Promoted kernel achieves success_rate < 0.80 on held-out resource-B identifiers on the real localhost stdlib-HTTP substrate; (4) Known-negative refusal rate < 0.95 across the three categories, or any refusal lacks bound_action=null or a correctly categorized reason string; (5) The literal distill() baseline (confidence 0.5) achieves success_rate >= 0.20 on held-out parameterized tasks (indicating the confidence gate is not enforced).

baselines.description: Current shipped kernel behavior: only literal distill() with hardcoded confidence 0.5, no distill_parameterized. On parameterized tasks with min_confidence=0.8, resolve returns EXPLORE/UNKNOWN. This is the causal-attribution ablation control proving the parameterized path is necessary.

The audited kernel from EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064/EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 (git blob b15ed848, sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72) running in the experiment harness. This is the positive reference implementation that demonstrated 12/15 held-out success and 15/15 known-negative refusal. Used to verify the promoted kernel matches the audited behavior.

null_control.description: Known-negative test cases covering three refusal categories: (1) out-of-support identifiers (e.g., item-999, user-xyz); (2) wrong intent (e.g., 'delete' intent against 'read' mechanism); (3) missing required parameter (resolve called without 'id' param). All must return bound_action=null with non-empty reason string correctly categorizing the refusal type. Expected: 100% refusal rate with correct categorization.

measurement_validity: Credential-free: No model API keys, no browser, no external network. Pure localhost stdlib http.server.

Real promotion path: The experiment executes the actual sanctioned promotion workflow (scripts/finalize_lane.py promotion logic or equivalent) to copy the audited kernel into src/spider/kernel.py, not a simulated or manual copy.

Substrate identical to audited carrier: Real localhost stdlib-HTTP server with 3 resource types (items, users, orders) x 10 identifiers each (training A: 001-005, held-out B: 006-010, out-of-support C: 999, xyz). Deterministic, fixed seed.

Honest unit accounting: Per-trajectory counters for model_calls, model_tokens, retrieval_calls, verification_calls, repair_attempts, http_requests, latency_ms. Model counters MUST be zero (credential-free). Counters fire on real mechanism execution.
Causal attribution: B-LITERAL-KERNEL baseline (confidence 0.5 < 0.8) isolates parameterized path contribution. Promoted kernel vs audited carrier behavior compared on identical held-out tasks.
Known-negative detection: Three refusal categories each with distinct recorded reason and bound_action=null.
Deterministic substrate: Fixed seed, no stochastic server elements, single-threaded.
Promoted kernel is the SHIPPED kernel: After promotion, src/spider/kernel.py IS the treatment; no vendored copy, no harness substitution.

decision_rule.promotion: Sanctioned promotion completes: audited kernel code lands in src/spider/kernel.py, promotion validation passes (verdict.promote_to_product=false for this experiment since it's a prerequisite landing, not a product feature ship), and the promoted kernel is importable and runnable.
decision_rule.primary: Promoted kernel achieves success_rate >= 0.80 on held-out resource-B identifiers (15 tasks: 5 per type x 3 types) on the real HTTP substrate.
decision_rule.known_negative: Known-negative refusal rate >= 0.95 across all three categories (out-of-support, wrong-intent, missing-parameter). Each refusal must have bound_action=null and a non-empty reason string correctly categorizing the refusal type.
decision_rule.causal_attribution: B-LITERAL-KERNEL baseline (current shipped kernel before promotion, confidence 0.5 < min_confidence 0.8) achieves success_rate < 0.20 on held-out resource-B parameterized tasks.
decision_rule.fidelity: Promoted kernel behavior matches B-AUDITED-CARRIER on the same held-out tasks (success_rate within 0.05, identical refusal patterns).

overall_outcome.FALSIFIES: PROMOTION fails OR PRIMARY fails OR KNOWN_NEGATIVE fails
overall_outcome.MIXED: PROMOTION and PRIMARY pass but KNOWN_NEGATIVE or CAUSAL_ATTRIBUTION or FIDELITY fails
overall_outcome.MEASUREMENT_INVALID: Substrate fails to start, promotion infrastructure failure, or non-determinism detected

product_consequence_positive: B1 blocker REMOVED: The shipped kernel (src/spider/kernel.py) now contains a live, executable parameterized mechanism path (distill_parameterized -> resolve -> execute) with a verified known-negative refusal certificate. C-PARAM-INHERIT advances from EXPERIMENTAL toward VALIDATED. The critical path for the four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT benchmark (pending model credential and non-ceiling task bank) is cleared of the kernel promotion dependency. The kernel parameterization becomes a behavior-bound shipped capability, not a synthetic-fixture or vendored-harness artifact.
product_consequence_negative: B1 blocker PERSISTS: The sanctioned promotion path fails, or the promoted kernel does not demonstrate the required behavior on the real substrate. C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL without a shipped executable carrier. The four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT benchmark remains blocked on B1 in addition to B2/B3. Product lane must not promote kernel parameterization to product core. The kernel engineering gap must be diagnosed and re-attempted.
estimated_cost: Very low: Pure localhost stdlib http.server, no model API calls, no browser, no external network. ~50 HTTP requests per arm x 3 arms x 20 test identifiers = ~3000 requests total. Single-threaded, deterministic, completes in < 60 seconds. Promotion step is a file copy + validation. No GPU, no cloud costs.
expected_information_gain: High: This is the first experiment to land the audited parameterized kernel into the SHIPPED path via the sanctioned promotion workflow and verify it works as the actual shipping code (not a harness copy). It directly addresses the Global Research Director's highest-leverage product action: removing B1, the first of three verified blockers. A positive result establishes the shipped kernel parameterization as a real-substrate capability with a known-negative certificate; a negative result bounds the promotion/engineering gap.

freeze_eligibility_justifications.decision_rule_reachability: The decision rule has four independently checkable clauses (promotion, primary, known_negative, causal_attribution, fidelity) with explicit pass/fail thresholds. No clause depends on unobservable quantities. The overall outcome mapping is exhaustive and deterministic.
freeze_eligibility_justifications.measurement_prerequisites: The audited carrier implementation exists at a known git blob (b15ed848, sha256 718efa6a...). The sanctioned promotion path is implemented in scripts/finalize_lane.py (promote_to_product logic for Product lane). The credential-free HTTP substrate is implemented and tested in EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064 (harness/substrate.py). All prerequisites are present and verified.
freeze_eligibility_justifications.baseline_identifiability: B-LITERAL-KERNEL is the current shipped src/spider/kernel.py at base_sha 6b4a1f7b18e84015e1765965081f2a8e97d3ba27 (git blob cfec98660b0277ccbf295e8a4119e8d81ddccf50). It is frozen by the request.json base_sha and can be identifiably retrieved. B-AUDITED-CARRIER is frozen by git blob hash b15ed848.
freeze_eligibility_justifications.control_sensitivity: NC-KNOWN-NEGATIVE provides three distinct refusal categories with specific expected reason strings. The audited carrier achieved 15/15 correct refusals. The control is sensitive: a broken support inference or missing parameter check will produce incorrect reasons or EXECUTABLE instead of EXPLORE/UNKNOWN. B-LITERAL-KERNEL is sensitive: if the confidence gate is not enforced, it would incorrectly pass parameterized tasks.
freeze_eligibility_justifications.treatment_liveness: The treatment IS the audited carrier (EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064 result: 12/15 held-out success, 15/15 known-negative refusal, causal attribution PASS). It has already been demonstrated live and executable on the real substrate. Promotion is a code-transfer operation, not a new mechanism invention.
freeze_eligibility_justifications.freeze_artifacts_bound: All mutable local dependencies are enumerated in freeze_artifacts below with repository-relative paths. The freezer will hash them into freeze.json.artifact_hashes.
